title: Networking: advanced NetworkManager
objective: Manage profiles, multiple addresses, routes and device behaviour with nmcli.

questions.q: Where does NetworkManager on RHEL 9/10 store connection profiles by default?
questions.explain: The old ifcfg format still works but keyfiles are the default; run `nmcli con reload` after hand-editing.

questions.q: What does the `+` prefix do in `nmcli con mod eth0 +ipv4.addresses 10.0.0.5/24`?
options: Appends to the list property without removing existing values
questions.explain: Use `-` to remove one item; no prefix replaces the entire list.

questions.q: A change made with `nmcli con mod` takes effect when you:
questions.explain: Editing over SSH and changing the IP drops your session; use the console.

questions.q: Which property makes a connection come up automatically at boot?
questions.explain: Check it with `nmcli -f connection.autoconnect con show <name>`.

questions.q: How do you add a static route "reach 192.168.50.0/24 via 192.168.1.254" to a profile?
questions.explain: This route persists in the profile, unlike a bare `ip route add`.

questions.q: What does `ipv4.route-metric` control?
options: The priority of this connection's routes (lower wins) when multiple paths exist
questions.explain: Useful when a host has two uplinks and you prefer one.

questions.q: Show all connection profiles NetworkManager knows about.
questions.explain: `nmcli device status` shows devices and which profile each uses.

questions.q: Add a second IPv4 address 10.0.0.5/24 to the profile "eth0" without removing the first.
questions.explain: Apply it with `nmcli con up eth0`.

questions.q: Create a brand-new static connection profile "lab" on device eth1.
accept: nmcli con add con-name lab type ethernet ifname eth1 ipv4.addresses 192.168.99.10/24 ipv4.method manual
questions.explain: Add `ipv4.gateway` and `ipv4.dns` as the task requires.

questions.q: Reload connection files after editing a keyfile by hand.
questions.explain: Then `nmcli con up <name>` to apply.

labs.title: Multi-homed host (exam-plus)
labs.scenario: Give one interface two IPv4 addresses, a static route to a remote subnet, and make it all persist and autoconnect. Verify after a reboot.
steps: nmcli con mod eth0 connection.autoconnect yes
verify: ip -br a; ip route | grep 192.168.50; reboot and re-check

labs.title: Switch between two profiles on one NIC
labs.scenario: Create a static profile and keep the DHCP one; switch between them and confirm the active address each time.
steps: nmcli con add con-name static-lab type ethernet ifname eth0 ipv4.addresses 172.16.0.10/24 ipv4.method manual
nmcli con up static-lab && ip -br a
nmcli con up "System eth0" && ip -br a
verify: nmcli con show --active shows which profile is live each time

labs.title: Prefer one uplink with route metrics
labs.scenario: On a host with two connections, set route metrics so one is preferred, and confirm the default route uses it.
steps: nmcli con up primary; nmcli con up backup
verify: ip route shows the default via the lower-metric (primary) connection

labs.title: Inspect a profile in detail
labs.scenario: Show all IPv4 settings of a connection and the DNS it applies.
steps: nmcli dev show eth0 | grep -i dns
verify: you can read the profile's addresses, gateway, routes and DNS

title: Networking: link aggregation (bonding)
objective: Combine NICs into a bond for redundancy or throughput.

questions.q: What is network bonding?
options: Combining two or more NICs into one logical interface for redundancy or bandwidth
questions.explain: On RHEL 9/10 use bonding; the older "teaming" (teamd) was removed.

questions.q: Which bond mode gives simple failover with one active NIC at a time?
questions.explain: active-backup needs no special switch support; 802.3ad (LACP) needs a configured switch.

questions.q: What does the miimon bond option do?
options: Sets how often (ms) to check link state for failover
questions.explain: e.g. miimon=100 checks every 100 ms.

questions.q: In a bond, the member interfaces are called:
questions.explain: Each port is its own connection profile with the bond as its controller/master.

questions.q: Which file shows a bond's live status and active port?
questions.explain: It lists the mode, each port's link state, and the currently active port.

questions.q: Why use active-backup mode for a server with two switches?
options: It survives a switch or cable failure with no special switch config
questions.explain: Redundancy without LACP; throughput bonding (802.3ad) needs switch support.

questions.q: Create a bond interface bond0 in active-backup mode with miimon 100.
accept: nmcli con add type bond con-name bond0 ifname bond0 bond.options "mode=active-backup,miimon=100"
questions.explain: Give it an IP with `ipv4.addresses`/`ipv4.method manual` as the task requires.

questions.q: Add the NIC eth1 as a port of bond0.
accept: nmcli con add type ethernet con-name bond0-port1 ifname eth1 master bond0
questions.explain: Repeat for eth2 as bond0-port2; the ports have no IP of their own.

questions.q: Show the live status and active port of bond0.
questions.explain: Also `nmcli device status` shows the bond and its ports.

labs.title: Build a redundant bond (exam-plus)
labs.scenario: Create bond0 (active-backup, miimon=100) with a static IP, add two NICs as ports, bring it up, and verify failover status.
steps: nmcli con add type bond con-name bond0 ifname bond0 bond.options "mode=active-backup,miimon=100" ipv4.addresses 192.168.100.20/24 ipv4.method manual
nmcli con add type ethernet con-name bond0-p1 ifname eth1 master bond0
nmcli con add type ethernet con-name bond0-p2 ifname eth2 master bond0
verify: ip -br a shows bond0 with the IP; the bonding file lists two ports and one active

labs.title: Test bond failover
labs.scenario: Bring down the currently active port and confirm the bond fails over to the other, keeping connectivity.
steps: cat /proc/net/bonding/bond0      # active port switched to p2
verify: connectivity survives; the active port changed

labs.title: Persist and reboot-test the bond
labs.scenario: Ensure the bond and both ports autoconnect and survive a reboot.
steps: nmcli con mod bond0 connection.autoconnect yes
verify: after reboot: ip -br a shows bond0 up with two ports

labs.title: Inspect bond configuration
labs.scenario: Show the bond's options and each port's controller relationship.
verify: you can read the mode/miimon and confirm the ports belong to bond0

title: Networking: advanced firewalld
objective: Use zones, rich rules, masquerading and port forwarding.

questions.q: A firewalld "zone" represents:
options: A trust level with its own rules, bound to interfaces or source addresses
questions.explain: Common zones: public, trusted, drop, internal, dmz.

questions.q: What does a rich rule let you do that a simple service/port rule cannot?
options: Match on source address, log, rate-limit, and accept/reject/drop with fine control
questions.explain: Rich rules combine source, service/port, action and logging in one rule.

questions.q: What does `firewall-cmd --add-masquerade` enable?
options: Source NAT, so traffic from an internal network is translated to the host's address
questions.explain: Needed when the host routes traffic for a private network to the internet.

questions.q: A firewalld port-forward rule sends traffic arriving on one port to:
options: Another port (and optionally another host) — e.g. 80 -> 8080
questions.explain: Use `--add-forward-port=port=80:proto=tcp:toport=8080`.

questions.q: Which command permanently rejects SSH only from 192.168.50.0/24?
options: firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.50.0/24" service name="ssh" reject'
questions.explain: `man firewalld.richlanguage` has copyable examples for the exam.

questions.q: What is the difference between "reject" and "drop" in a rule?
options: reject replies that the connection is refused; drop silently discards it
questions.explain: drop makes the host appear offline to that source.

questions.q: Add a rich rule that logs and drops all traffic from 10.0.0.66.
accept: firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="10.0.0.66" log prefix="DROP66 " level="info" drop'
questions.explain: Reload after; check /var/log/messages or the journal for the log prefix.

questions.q: Enable masquerading (source NAT) in the current zone permanently.
questions.explain: Then `firewall-cmd --reload`.

questions.q: Forward incoming TCP port 80 to port 8080 on this host.
questions.explain: Requires masquerade for forwarding to another host.

questions.q: Put the source 192.168.10.0/24 into the trusted zone permanently.
questions.explain: `--get-active-zones` shows which sources/interfaces map to which zone.

labs.title: Zone-based access control (exam-plus)
labs.scenario: Put your management subnet in the "internal" zone with ssh allowed, keep "public" for everything else with only http, and verify.
verify: firewall-cmd --zone=internal --list-all and --zone=public --list-all match the intent

labs.title: Rich rule with logging
labs.scenario: Reject SSH from one subnet with a logged rich rule, test from that subnet, and read the log.
steps: firewall-cmd --permanent --add-rich-rule='rule family="ipv4" source address="192.168.50.0/24" service name="ssh" log prefix="SSH-REJ " level="info" reject'
# from a host in 192.168.50.0/24:  ssh <this-host>   -> refused
verify: the connection is rejected and logged

labs.title: Port forwarding
labs.scenario: Make the host accept web traffic on port 80 but serve it from a service on 8080, using firewalld.
verify: traffic to :80 is served by the :8080 service

labs.title: Save runtime rules and audit
labs.scenario: Add a couple of runtime-only rules, make them permanent, and produce a full audit of every zone.
verify: the https rule persists and you have a full zone audit

title: Networking: nftables
objective: Understand and write basic nftables rulesets (the modern firewall backend).

questions.q: What is nftables?
options: The modern Linux packet-filtering framework that replaces iptables (and backs firewalld)
questions.explain: On RHEL, firewalld uses the nftables backend by default.

questions.q: In nftables, the top-level container of chains is a:
options: Table (with a family such as inet, ip, ip6)
questions.explain: A table holds chains; chains hold rules.

questions.q: A base chain must declare its:
questions.explain: e.g. `type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop;`

questions.q: Which command shows the entire active nftables ruleset?
questions.explain: Save it to /etc/nftables.conf to make it persistent via the nftables service.

questions.q: How do you make an nftables ruleset load at boot on RHEL?
options: Put it in /etc/nftables.conf (or an included file) and enable nftables.service
questions.explain: `systemctl enable --now nftables` loads /etc/sysconfig/nftables.conf includes.

questions.q: Why generally NOT mix raw nftables rules with firewalld on the same host?
options: firewalld manages its own nftables rules; hand rules can conflict or be overwritten
questions.explain: Pick one manager per host; for the RHCSA, firewalld is the expected tool.

questions.q: Show the complete active nftables ruleset.
questions.explain: With firewalld running, you will see the firewalld-generated tables here.

questions.q: Create a new table named filter in the inet family.
questions.explain: inet covers both IPv4 and IPv6.

questions.q: Add an input base chain that drops by default to the inet filter table.
accept: nft add chain inet filter input '{ type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop; }'
questions.explain: Then add accept rules for loopback, established traffic and SSH.

questions.q: List the ruleset of just the inet filter table.
questions.explain: Useful to review one table without the whole ruleset.

labs.title: Build a minimal nftables firewall (lab, non-firewalld host)
labs.scenario: On a test host NOT using firewalld, build a small ruleset: default-drop input, allow loopback, established, and SSH; then verify.
steps: nft add chain inet filter input '{ type filter hook input priority 0; policy drop; }'
nft add rule inet filter input iif lo accept
nft add rule inet filter input ct state established,related accept
nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 22 accept
verify: you can still SSH in and other ports are dropped

labs.title: Persist an nftables ruleset
labs.scenario: Save your working ruleset to /etc/nftables.conf and enable it at boot.
steps: # ensure the file starts with: #!/usr/sbin/nft -f  and  flush ruleset
verify: after reboot: nft list ruleset shows your rules

labs.title: See what firewalld generates
labs.scenario: On a firewalld host, view the nftables rules firewalld created, to understand the relationship.
verify: you can see firewalld's rules expressed as nftables

labs.title: Add and delete a rule by handle
labs.scenario: Add a rule, list with handles, then delete that specific rule by its handle.
steps: nft add rule inet filter input tcp dport 8080 accept
nft -a list table inet filter        # shows # handle N
nft delete rule inet filter input handle <N>
verify: the 8080 rule is gone; the rest remain

title: Networking: bridges, VLANs and routing
objective: Create bridges and VLAN interfaces and manage static routing.

questions.q: A software bridge (br0) is commonly used to:
options: Connect virtual machines/containers to the physical network as if on the same switch
questions.explain: VMs attach to the bridge and appear on the LAN directly.

questions.q: A VLAN interface (eth0.10) lets one physical NIC:
options: Carry multiple isolated networks tagged with 802.1Q VLAN IDs
questions.explain: The switch port must be a trunk allowing that VLAN.

questions.q: Which nmcli command creates VLAN 10 on device eth0?
options: nmcli con add type vlan con-name vlan10 ifname eth0.10 dev eth0 id 10
nmcli con add type ethernet vlan 10
questions.explain: The interface name convention is device.vlanid (eth0.10).

questions.q: A static route added with `ip route add` (not via nmcli) is:
options: Lost on reboot / connection restart unless stored in the profile
questions.explain: Persist routes with `nmcli con mod ... +ipv4.routes`.

questions.q: Policy routing with `ip rule` lets you:
options: Choose a routing table based on source address or other selectors
questions.explain: Advanced multi-uplink setups use multiple routing tables plus ip rule.

questions.q: To let a Linux host forward packets between networks you must:
questions.explain: Set it in /etc/sysctl.d/ and apply with `sysctl --system`.

questions.q: Create a bridge br0 with nmcli.
accept: nmcli con add type bridge con-name br0 ifname br0
questions.explain: Then attach a NIC: `nmcli con add type ethernet con-name br0-port ifname eth1 master br0`.

questions.q: Create VLAN 20 on eth0 with a static IP.
accept: nmcli con add type vlan con-name vlan20 ifname eth0.20 dev eth0 id 20 ipv4.addresses 192.168.20.5/24 ipv4.method manual
questions.explain: Bring it up with `nmcli con up vlan20`.

questions.q: Enable IPv4 forwarding right now (runtime).
questions.explain: Persist it in /etc/sysctl.d/99-forward.conf with `net.ipv4.ip_forward=1`.

questions.q: Add a persistent static route to 10.10.0.0/16 via 192.168.1.254 on profile eth0.
questions.explain: Apply with `nmcli con up eth0`; verify with `ip route`.

labs.title: Create a bridge for VMs (exam-plus)
labs.scenario: Build br0, attach a physical NIC to it, give the bridge a static IP, and confirm it carries the IP instead of the NIC.
steps: nmcli con add type bridge con-name br0 ifname br0 ipv4.addresses 192.168.1.30/24 ipv4.gateway 192.168.1.1 ipv4.method manual
nmcli con add type ethernet con-name br0-port ifname eth1 master br0
verify: br0 holds the IP; eth1 is a port of the bridge; connectivity works

labs.title: VLAN interface
labs.scenario: Create VLAN 30 on eth0 with its own subnet and verify tagging works to the gateway.
steps: nmcli con add type vlan con-name vlan30 ifname eth0.30 dev eth0 id 30 ipv4.addresses 192.168.30.5/24 ipv4.method manual
ip -d link show eth0.30 | grep -i vlan
verify: the vlan interface exists, is tagged 30, and reaches its gateway

labs.title: Turn a host into a router
labs.scenario: Enable persistent IP forwarding and add the routes so a host bridges two subnets, then confirm forwarding is on.
verify: net.ipv4.ip_forward = 1 and traffic can route between the two attached subnets

labs.title: Persistent static routing
labs.scenario: Add two persistent routes to a profile and confirm they appear in the routing table after reactivation.
verify: both routes are present and survive a reboot

title: Networking: troubleshooting and diagnostics
objective: Diagnose connectivity, ports, DNS and performance methodically.

questions.q: What is a sound order for troubleshooting "I can't reach a server"?
options: Link -> IP/route -> gateway -> DNS -> the remote port/service
questions.explain: Work up the stack: is the link up, do I have an IP and route, can I reach the gateway, does the name resolve, is the port open?

questions.q: Which command shows listening TCP/UDP ports with the owning process?
questions.explain: t=TCP, u=UDP, l=listening, p=process, n=numeric.

questions.q: `ping` succeeds to an IP but a website fails by name. The likely problem is:
questions.explain: Test with `dig <name>` or `getent hosts <name>`.

questions.q: Which tool combines traceroute and ping to show per-hop loss over time?
questions.explain: mtr is excellent for spotting a flaky hop.

questions.q: `ethtool eth0` is used to check:
options: Link speed, duplex and whether the link is detected on a NIC
questions.explain: A half-duplex or down link explains many "slow/no network" issues.

questions.q: Where do you look for NetworkManager errors during troubleshooting?
questions.explain: Add `-b` for this boot, `-f` to follow live while you reactivate a connection.

questions.q: `getent hosts server1` is useful because it:
options: Resolves a name using the system's full nsswitch order (files + DNS), like real apps do
questions.explain: It reflects what applications actually see, unlike a raw DNS query.

questions.q: Show all interfaces, their state and IPs in one short line each.
questions.explain: `ip -br link` shows just link state; great for a quick health check.

questions.q: Show the routing table including the default gateway.
questions.explain: The default route line (`default via ...`) is the gateway.

questions.q: Test whether TCP port 443 is open on a remote host without extra tools.
questions.explain: `nc -z` scans without sending data; authorized targets only.

questions.q: Follow NetworkManager's log live while you reactivate a connection.
questions.explain: In another terminal run `nmcli con up <name>` and watch the messages.

labs.title: Methodical connectivity triage (exam-plus)
labs.scenario: A host cannot reach an internal server by name. Work the stack: check link, IP/route, gateway, DNS, then the remote port, and identify the failing layer.
steps: ip -br a; ip -br link            # link + IP
getent hosts server1              # does the name resolve?
nc -zv server1 22                 # is the service port open?
verify: you can state which layer is broken and the fix

labs.title: DNS troubleshooting
labs.scenario: Diagnose a name that will not resolve: check the resolver, query directly, and confirm the search domain.
verify: you can tell whether it is a resolver, record, or search-domain problem

labs.title: Port and service check
labs.scenario: Find what is listening locally, then verify a remote host's port is reachable from here.
verify: you know which local ports listen and whether the remote port is open

labs.title: Capture and read traffic for a stubborn issue
labs.scenario: On an authorized host, capture a few packets of a failing connection to see where it stops.
steps: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -n host 192.168.1.50 and port 443 -c 20
# look for SYN with no SYN-ACK (blocked/no service) vs RST (refused)
verify: you can interpret the handshake to locate the failure

labs.title: Link-layer check
labs.scenario: Confirm a NIC's link, speed and duplex, and review recent driver/link messages.
verify: you can confirm the physical link is healthy or spot a flapping NIC
